As of 325 AM Friday... 

KEY MESSAGE 1... Record heat today will be swept offshore by a 
strong cold front and following sharply cooler and wet conditions 
that will develop tonight into Sat.

An increasingly-phased and high amplitude trough, apparent in GOES-E 
WV satellite data from nrn Hudson Bay to the cntl High Plains, will 
pivot across the ern US through late Sat-Sat night. A vigorous upper 
jet and front will accompany the trough, with a zone of strong and 
deep ascent that will overspread cntl NC tonight-Sat. 

At the surface, a backdoor front has drifted into the nrn Sandhills 
and the nw Piedmont this morning, about 20-30 miles farther swwd 
than previously forecast. While low overcast has developed within 
the pos-trontal regime and would typically slow/retard subsequent 
nwd retreat of the front, cooling behind the front and the related 
frontal inversion are not pronounced. Additionally, the MSL pressure 
pattern surrounding the front over the srn Middle Atlantic, between 
a 1021 mb high drifting off the coast of New England and a ~1019 mb 
one off the South Atlantic coast, appear to be reaching equilibrium 
this morning. As such, it remains likely that the front will retreat 
quickly nwd with the onset of diurnal heating, in strengthening flow 
and mass response ahead of the intense trough aloft and a related 
surface cyclone now deepening across MI. A pre-frontal, Appalachian-
lee trough will sharpen across the nw Piedmont this afternoon and 
precede a strong cold front that will sweep across cntl NC tonight. 

A growing warm sector throughout cntl NC today will yield yet 
another day of record temperatures mostly between 85-90 F, 
accompanied by a gusty swly surface wind that will develop with 
daytime heating/mixing by midday-early afternoon. 

Scattered showers are likely to develop along the pre-frontal trough 
over the nw Piedmont by ~21-22Z, in a regime of weak MLCAPE of 
generally less than 500 J/kg, but where instability will be 
relatively maximized as cooling temperatures aloft edge east of the 
Appalachians. The band of showers will spread ewd and across the 
remainder of cntl NC this evening, along and immediately following 
the passing cold front. Anafrontal precipitation character will 
become increasingly stratiform and probably blossom after midnight, 
as the intense mid and upper-level trough and jet, and deep zone of 
Fgen, overspread the Carolinas. 

The precipitation band will then edge from west to east across cntl 
NC during the day Sat, with storm total rainfall amounts mostly 
between a quarter and half inch. It will otherwise turn sharply 
cooler, with highs Sat 25-30 F below those of today and about 10-15 
F below average. A strong and gusty nly wind will make it feel even 
cooler. 


KEY MESSAGE 2... Cold Saturday and Sunday nights, with some patchy 
frost Sun morning and again Mon morning. 

Aloft, it is looking increasingly likely a low will close off within 
the parent trough as it tracks sewd across the region and offshore 
Sat/Sat night, though there remain differences wrt where and when 
that will occur. The low will likely sit/meander near or just off 
the Carolina/mid-Atlantic coast through much of the week. At the 
surface, the ~1036 mb high should lift newd from the OH Valley to 
the Canadian Maritimes Sat night through Sun night, while the ridge 
continues to extend swwd across the region. A low is expected to 
develop offshore, along the front, on Sat before cutting off from 
the parent trough and deepening as it meanders off the Southeast 
US/Carolina coast through at least Sun night, possibly through much 
of the week. However, a good bit of uncertainty remains wrt to this 
low and its impacts for central NC. Expect breezy conditions on Sun, 
with a strong pressure gradient between the deepening low offshore 
and the ridge over the area. The LLJ could remain quite stout on the 
back (NW) side of the low offshore through Sun night, with gusts of 
25-35 kts possible with mixing on Sun, highest east. The jet may be 
stronger overnight (25-40 kts) both nights and over a much larger 
area, but those stronger winds are generally not expected to mix 
down to the surface. Still, some gusts of 15-25 kts cannot be ruled 
out Sun night given the latest guidance showing a little mixing 
overnight. 

There remains a fair amount of spread in the statistical guidance 
between high and low members for temperatures from Sat night onward, 
given the uncertainty wrt the low offshore and subsequent impacts. 
For highs, Sunday should be the coolest day, with highs in the mid 
50s to around 60 degrees expected. Highs should rebound a bit on 
Mon, but still remain below normal, with low to mid 60s forecast. 
For lows, with continued breezy conditions, generally decreasing 
cloud cover, and low-level thicknesses around 1320 dam Sat night, 
will err on the mean for lows, ranging from mid-upper 30s NW to mid
